title: impulse-sprint-telemetry-brief
content:
Context:
This is a short personal scratchpad documenting an "impulse sprint" experiment: extremely short (100-500ms) high-qps spikes injected against a single GPU inference shard to study warm-cache priming, proxy buffering, and scheduler reaction. Trying to capture quick telemetry, hypothesis, and action items rather than a polished report.

Goal:
- Characterize system behavior for 200ms and 500ms bursts at 2x, 5x, and 10x baseline QPS.
- See which layer dominates cold-path latency during the impulse window: client, edge proxy, ingress queue, serving runtime, or GPU kernel startup.
- Collect high-frequency histograms (1ms bins where possible) to locate microsecond-level regressions.

High-level hypothesis:
- Very short spikes (<< warmup window) will primarily amplify edge/ingress queuing and the runtime scheduling jitter, not model KV cache misses.
- For 200ms impulses the majority of p99 penalty will be due to proxy batching and request coalescing latency.

Test matrix (client replay):
- Model: open-{smallbert}-v2 (sequence len 256), single shard CPU+GPU hybrid, quantized float16.
- Baseline: steady 50 qps sustained for 60s prior to spike.
- Impulse durations: 100ms, 200ms, 500ms.
- Impulse QPS multipliers: x2, x5, x10.
- Clients: 8 concurrent runners from 3 regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1) to test cross-regional aggregation at edge.
- Repeats: 8 runs per cell.

Commands used (client-side harness snippets):
- warm baseline: ./replay --qps=50 --duration=60 --concurrency=8 --model=smallbert --seq=256
- impulse: ./replay --burst=500 --burst-duration-ms=200 --baseline-qps=50 --concurrency=8 --region=us-west1
- telemetry sampling: ./telemetry-dump --freq-ms=10 --histogram-bins-ms=1 --out=run123.hf

What I captured:
- Request-level histograms (client-side) with 1ms resolution (raw).
- Edge-proxy ingress queue length (10ms samples).
- Serving runtime scheduler trace (coalescing windows, time to first kernel launch).
- GPU occupancy and first-kernel spinup time from nvidia-smi + custom loader logs.
- KV-cache hit ratio computed by instrumenting runtime (sampled 1000 requests/run).

Representative raw observations (200ms impulse @ x5):
- p50 client latency: baseline 28ms -> impulse 36ms (+8ms)
- p95 client latency: baseline 62ms -> impulse 210ms (+148ms)
- p99 client latency: baseline 112ms -> impulse 540ms (+428ms)
- edge-proxy queue depth: baseline <=2 -> impulse peaks 42 (10ms samples)
- runtime scheduling delay (time between request dequeue to kernel launch): median 6ms -> impulse median 18ms; 99th 210ms
- gpu first-kernel-for-request: spike observed in ~9% of impulse requests (duration 45-120ms extra)
- kv-cache hit rate: baseline 99.2% -> impulse 98.6% (small drop, not explanatory for large p99)

Interpretation notes:
- Large p95/p99 amplification correlates strongly with proxy queue depth spikes. That suggests proxy buffering + head-of-line blocking from the burst pattern.
- Runtime scheduling delay increase (median up by ~12ms) indicates lock contention or scheduling window growth when many requests arrive simultaneously.
- GPU kernel spinup (the 9%) accounts for a portion of p99 tail but not all; most of the extreme tail aligns with deferred scheduling rather than pure kernel cold-start.
- KV-cache drop small: implies not a content-miss issue for this model/sequence length.

Quick diagram (text):
Client -> Edge Proxy (in-flight queue) -> Ingress Shard (coalescer) -> Runtime Scheduler -> GPU Kernel -> Response
Observed dominant impedance: Edge Proxy queue and Runtime Scheduler interlock.

Interesting micro-behaviors:
- When edge queue > 20, we see a bimodal latency shape: a cohort that gets batched quickly (~30-80ms) and a cohort that waits for a coalescing window to finish and then suffers an extra 200-500ms delay.
- Coalescing window appears to be dynamic: at high queue depths it extends slightly (heuristic backpressure). Need to find config knob.
- Some proxy instances show higher variance than others — maybe heterogeneity in instance sizes or GC pauses on the proxy. Correlates with region (us-east1 worse than us-west1 in this run).

Short experiment notes (100ms impulse @ x10):
- Spiky p99s > 800ms observed in 2/8 runs. Edge queue peaked >120.
- GPU spinups higher (~17% of requests) due to request bursts exceeding warm-KV threshold and some micro-evictions.
- Observed ~3s long tail for a tiny fraction (0.02%) — traced to a transient event where the scheduler thread hit a safepoint while migrating a large batch. Need to correlate with runtime GC logs.

Potential configuration knobs to try next:
- Reduce proxy max coalescing window (ms) and measure effect on p95 vs p99. Hypothesis: smaller window reduces p99 at expense of throughput efficiency.
- Add early admission control at edge (soft drop or token-bucket smoothing for impulses) to stabilize ingress queue growth.
- Change runtime scheduler to use a pessimistic per-thread dequeue vs global-coalescer lock to reduce contention.
- Pre-warm GPU kernel pool during predicted impulse window by spawning a no-op kernel (cheap) to reduce first-kernel spinups.

Actionable next steps (short):
1) Re-run limited matrix with proxy coalescing window fixed to 8ms (current default ~20ms) for 200ms impulse x5. Collect the same telemetry. (Owner: me)
2) Add a light-weight periodic kernel ping (0.5s cadence) in a canary runtime to test warmup mitigation; run as A/B. (Owner: Ethan)
3) Correlate proxy GC logs for high-variance instances and check instance type metadata. (Owner: Maya)
4) File a perf ticket to investigate scheduler lock hold time during high dequeue bursts. (JIRA-ENG-4821)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does the coalescer window extend under load? Is that an explicit backpressure setting or emergent from our event-loop scheduling?
- Is there a sharp threshold of ingress queue after which kernel spinups spike? (Need higher resolution sweep around queue depth 20-60).
- Can we cheaply pre-allocate N cold kernels per shard without harming throughput?

Notes on measurement fidelity and caveats:
- Client-side clocks were NTP-synced but still showed up to 6ms drift between regions; histograms are aligned by request-id, not wall time, to minimize artifacts.
- Sampling rate: telemetry-dump at 10ms may under-sample microbursts <10ms; repeated with 1ms sampling next run if ingestion and storage can handle the volume.
- Runs affected by background noise from other tenants on shared infra in two runs; I'll mark those as noisy.

Quick TL;DR (for hallway sync):
- Short, high-amplitude spikes create p95/p99 tails mainly via edge-proxy queuing and runtime scheduling jitter, not KV cache misses.
- Knobs to try: tighten proxy coalescing window, early admission smoothing, and proactive kernel pre-warm.

Appendix: quick raw numbers table (sample run 2024-11-07 14:18 UTC)
- baseline qps 50: p50 28ms, p95 62ms, p99 112ms
- impulse 200ms x5: p50 36ms, p95 210ms, p99 540ms, edge-peak 42
- impulse 100ms x10: p50 40ms, p95 320ms, p99 820ms, edge-peak 128

End notes: leaving this here as a working scratchpad. Will iterate after the coalescing-window runs.

-- Nikhil
